Named violating input: a caused_by target ticket id that appears ONLY in a commit reachable from refs/remotes/origin/tickets (a ticket-event commit) and NOT from HEAD or refs/remotes/origin/<code-branch>
advisory.finding: No regression test covers the deliberate exclusion of the tickets branch from the caused_by upstream scan. upstream_branch_refs filters remote-tracking refs by the current branch-name suffix specifically so that refs/remotes/origin/tickets (the ticket event log, confirmed a real same-repo remote-tracking ref) is NOT walked; the referencing_commits docstring calls out that --all 'would walk one commit per ticket event — the wrong history'. If that branch-name filter regressed to returning all refs/remotes/ refs, a caused_by target whose id appears in a ticket-EVENT commit on refs/remotes/origin/tickets (but in no code commit) would be treated as 'referenced' and a genuinely commitless target would be wrongly ALLOWED — the exact misattribution the guard exists to prevent — and no test in the suite would fail.
scenarios: Default rebar store layout where the tickets event log shares the object database as refs/remotes/origin/tickets
A future refactor of upstream_branch_refs that drops the branch-name suffix filter
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a test on repo_with_history that creates a commit carrying `rebar-ticket: <culprit>` on the tickets branch (or update-ref refs/remotes/origin/tickets to a commit whose message references <culprit>), leaves HEAD and the code branch's remote-tracking ref without any such commit, and asserts rebar.link(bug, culprit, 'caused_by') raises RebarError and records no edge.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Pair `_refresh_remote_refs`'s coordinated `git fetch` with the same bounded `is_ref_cas_mismatch` retry both existing fetch entry points use, so a CAS lost to a non-rebar peer is retried rather than collapsed to 'unverifiable / allow'.
evidence: Shared resource: the checkout's remote-tracking refs / Git common-dir object DB — docs/concurrency.md:805 'two *uncoordinated* fetches against one common dir race: the loser fails `cannot lock ref ... is at <new> but expected <old>`'.

Second executor: the snapshot machinery's fetch (`rebar._snapshot.git_fetch.fetch_origin`, git_fetch.py:377-381 takes `fetch_coordination_lock(repo_root)`) and the sync fetch (sync.py:99 `with fetch_coordination_lock(tracker)`) advance the same `refs/remotes/*` the guard reads and writes.

Sibling accessor + guard #1: `rebar._store.sync._fetch` pairs the lock with a CAS retry — sync.py:98-104 `for attempt in range(1, _FETCH_CAS_ATTEMPTS + 1): with fetch_coordination_lock(tracker): ... if not git_outcome.is_ref_cas_mismatch(combined) or attempt == _FETCH_CAS_ATTEMPTS: return False`.

Sibling accessor + guard #2: `fetch_origin` pairs the lock with a CAS retry — git_fetch.py:411-415 `cas = is_ref_cas_mismatch(stderr) ... if cas: time.sleep(_CAS_RETRY_BACKOFF_S)`; docs/concurrency.md:822-824 'The lock removes the rebar-vs-rebar race; the retry absorbs a residual race with a non-rebar git peer, which never takes the lock.'

New twin omits the retry: link_revert.py:74-77 `with fetch_coordination_lock(code_root): proc = run_git_bounded(code_root, 'fetch', '--quiet', ...)` — single attempt, no `is_ref_cas_mismatch` check; run_git_bounded (gitutil.py:154-183) does not add CAS retry.

Unlocked-degradation window the retry is meant to net: git_locking.py:308-330 `_acquire_fetch_coord_flock` returns False after `_FETCH_COORD_WAIT_S` and the caller 'proceeds UNLOCKED (the bounded CAS retry is the net)'.

Harm (bounded/tolerant): lost CAS -> proc.returncode != 0 -> _refresh_remote_refs returns False (link_revert.py:81) -> `_absence_is_proven` line 148 `if probe == 'unknown' or not _refresh_remote_refs(code_root): return False` -> caused_by_refusal returns None -> link allowed for a target that genuinely has no referencing commit, contradicting the 'still refuse a genuinely commitless target after a refresh' contract asserted at tests/unit/test_caused_by_link_validation.py:test_a_refreshed_checkout_still_refuses_a_genuinely_commitless_target.
advisory.finding: New ref-updating fetch entry point `_refresh_remote_refs` takes `fetch_coordination_lock` but omits the bounded `is_ref_cas_mismatch` retry that both existing sibling fetch entry points pair with that lock, so a ref CAS lost to a concurrent non-rebar peer (or during the lock's unlocked-degradation window) fails the refresh and — via `_absence_is_proven` returning False — spuriously ALLOWS a `caused_by` link to a genuinely commitless target.
scenarios: A non-rebar git peer (or a concurrent snapshot/sync fetch that won the lock during this refresh's unlocked-degradation window) moves a remote-tracking ref while `_refresh_remote_refs` runs, so its single `git fetch` loses the ref CAS and returns non-zero.
MCP server under concurrent snapshot fetches while an agent creates a caused_by link to a commitless target.
advisory.suggested_fix: Route `_refresh_remote_refs` through the shared `sync._fetch`-style CAS-retry loop (bounded retry on `git_outcome.is_ref_cas_mismatch`) instead of a single `run_git_bounded('fetch')` call, matching the two-mechanism contract documented in docs/concurrency.md:814-828.
